item.title: Oral presentation at the International Ornithological Congress 2026
item.description:
I will give an oral presentation at the International Ornithological Congress (IOC 2026) in Mérida, Mexico, in the session Disease and environmental stressors.

Talk: Maternal mercury concentrations affect offspring mitochondrial function and growth When: Tuesday 1 December 2026, 16:15 Where: Room 26A

Mercury is a pervasive pollutant known to disrupt mitochondrial respiration, yet its effects on developing offspring in the wild are difficult to separate from genetic and environmental influences. In a two-year partial cross-fostering experiment in white-throated dippers (Cinclus cinclus), we exchanged nestlings between nests along a gradient of mercury exposure, allowing us to separate pre-hatching (maternal) from post-hatching exposure. The talk presents how maternal mercury relates to nestling mitochondrial respiration, oxidative stress, and growth.

I am grateful to the Swiss Society of Toxicology for a travel grant supporting my attendance.

item.title: Oral presentation at the Swiss Society of Toxicology Annual Meeting 2026
item.description:
My abstract, originally accepted as a poster, was selected for an oral presentation at the Swiss Society of Toxicology (SST) Annual Meeting 2026.

Talk: Maternal mercury exposure is associated with lower nestling mitochondrial respiration in a wild songbird: a cross-fostering experiment

The talk presented results from our partial cross-fostering experiment in white-throated dippers, showing that maternal mercury exposure was negatively associated with nestling mitochondrial respiration (OXPHOS), independently of the post-hatching rearing environment.

item.title: New paper in Biology Open: high-throughput measurement of mitochondrial metabolism
item.description:
Our paper with Cloé Hadjadji, Antoine Stier, and Pierre Bize has been published in Biology Open. We show that mitochondrial aerobic metabolism in avian red blood cells can be measured with a general-purpose plate reader, validated against high-resolution respirometry. Unlike dedicated respirometry instruments, which are costly and process few samples at a time, this high-throughput approach makes it feasible to measure mitochondrial function in large numbers of samples from wild birds.

Read the paper: Hadjadji, Ohse, Stier & Bize (2026), Biology Open 15, bio062712.

Cloé and I were also featured in the journal’s First Person series, where we discuss our research and career paths: read the interview.

item.title: Symposium on avian mitochondria at EOU 2025
item.description:
Together with Cloé Hadjadji and Pierre Bize, I convened the symposium Avian mitochondria: Powering ecology, evolution, and conservation at the 15th European Ornithologists’ Union (EOU) Conference in Bangor, UK, on 19 August 2025. The symposium brought together researchers studying mitochondrial function in birds across developmental, dietary, evolutionary, and environmental contexts.

Talks

  • Stefania Casagrande: Mitochondrial biology as a key mechanism linking reduced size and warmer nest temperatures in seabird nestlings
  • Elisa Thoral: Changes in diet composition affect energy metabolism at several biological scales in Japanese quail
  • Neal Dawson: Convergent and time-dependent evolutionary changes in mitochondrial function in high-altitude waterfowl
  • Pablo Salmón: Mitochondrial function and avian migration: lessons from a partial migrant
  • Molly Ohse: Cascading effects of mercury on mitochondrial traits and individual fitness in a wild population of European dippers
